hook: From {2011|twenty eleven} to {2023|twenty twenty-three}, India cut poverty from 57.7 to 16.1 percent.

beats.label: Estimated · $4.20/day line
beats.say: An estimated 496 million people moved above {$4.20|four dollars twenty} a day.

scene.note: World Bank estimates, 2011–12 CES and 2023–24 HCES

beats.label: Extreme poverty · $3.00/day
beats.say: Extreme poverty, at three dollars a day, fell from 27.1 to 2.6 percent.
beats.src: Summary, paragraph 1; Poverty at Different Lines table

beats.label: Main drivers, in the brief's words
beats.say: Mainly through consumption growth, more jobs, especially for women, and food subsidies.

scene.fact: +134 million employed, 2017–2023: nearly twice the growth of the working-age population

beats.label: $4.20/day line · 2023
beats.say: Rural poverty is 19.3 percent. Urban is 8.6.

beats.label: of India's poor · Uttar Pradesh to West Bengal
beats.say: And about 57 percent of the poor live in one belt, from Uttar Pradesh to West Bengal.

beats.label: Top 10% vs bottom 10% of workers
beats.say: Gaps remain. The top ten percent of workers earn about 13 times the bottom ten percent.

beats.label: Projected · $4.20/day line
beats.say: By {2028|twenty twenty-eight}, poverty is projected at 12.1 percent. The brief warns that some gains may reflect better measurement.

scene.caveat: Part of the 2022–24 gain likely reflects better measurement. The surveys likely understate inequality.

outro: Source: World Bank, India Poverty and Equity Brief, October {2026|twenty twenty-six}.

end.title: Poverty fell fast. Gaps remain.
end.source: World Bank, Poverty & Equity Brief: India, October 2026
